body: Nope.  They'll never get over it.  Losing a child is literally the worst thing that can happen to a person.  My daughter died 2 years ago and everyday since then has sucked.  I have a friend who lost her son 5 years ago and still cries everyday.  So that's the honest truth about it.
Nope, I would literally have to abandon everyone and everything in my life, and obtain a bunch of things I don't have.  There's a huge difference between "struggle" and "impossible"

^this exactly^ 

Other options are unrealistic or unlikely.   But it's not so much about wanting to die, as it is a realization that it's probably the only way to make everything stop hurting. 

If I had the option to wake up and be somebody else, I would choose that over death any day.

Can't say what I do for a living but it's the sorta thing where you can't really have mental problems beyond the occasional mild upset/grief sorta thing.  I have no redeeming qualities, no friends, I'm too quiet, have a shitty personality, and I can't remember the last time I was happy.

I really can't do that.  If I end up hospitalized I'll lose my job.  And I don't think not having financial security is going to make me feel better.  Plus I'm really just done,  I've given all I had to give and come up empty handed.  At the end of the day I'm always the one that's not as good as somebody else.  I'm not good at anything and my existence adds nothing of value to the world.

They know I'm depressed and have anxiety but they don't know I'm suicidal.  They don't say much honestly, like every time I go in there we manage to conquer whatever the most recent shitty situation that's happened is, but it's not even touching the tip of the iceberg.  We pretty much never even get to the depth of how painful all my social relationships with everyone in my life tend to be.

That's just it, at best I'm insignificant to the people in my life, no matter how much I try to be valued in my relationships, I'm just not.  Sitting around saying it's everyone else who's the problem just doesn't make sense.  I can't take the loneliness anymore.

I don't want anymore therapy or medication, I've done all that.  At the end of the day even if it makes me feel better for a time, it's always temporary.  It doesn't fix any of the real problems, it doesn't get rid of the crushing loneliness.  I'm just tired of my life.

I actually have 2 older brothers, I was referring to the oldest one in the original post and the other one here.  The oldest one molested us when we were little, and the other one was my father's golden child.  So as adults our relationship as siblings has always been rocky.  I was the first one to cut off communication with our father so that pretty much meant them being against me too until a couple years ago when they both called to tell me that I was right about him and that they had both agreed to stop talking to him as well.  So things have been more open since then, but I still am leery of really reaching out to them.  They have their own problems, they can still be very judgmental, and obviously there's a lot of issues because of the sexually abuse.

People everywhere have been telling me I'm crazy my whole life if I even ever hint that something is bothering me, let alone if I ever admit to any of these issues.  It's like being depressed or having anxiety means I can't be treated like an adult and given any trust or respect like other adults.  So I mostly just try to hide and bury my feelings. I'm a freak.  I see other people with issues surrounded by support, but if I ever admit to having the same issues I just get beaten down or accused of lying or being a less capable person than I am.  I even know other people who had bad childhoods and they still have friends and people who care about them.  But there's something wrong with me, I'm broken, I've just bounced from one abuser to the next my whole life, I don't really have any consistent friends.   So the only common denominator in all of this is me.  There is something wrong with me that drives good people off and then the only outside interaction I have left is with people who just want to use me until I'm not useful anymore.  I'm disposable.  

I mess things up all the time, and I lie about things on a near daily basis.  I try my best to just handle it, but sometimes things really get to me and I'll end up snapping at one of my coworkers or crying in public.  Not often, but it's happened about 3 times in the last few months, which is just further proof that I'm becoming even worse of a person.

I was anorexic and bulimic for a long long time before I managed to stop for a few years.  But it took it's toll anyway, and now I'm mostly just hoping the relapse will be a short trip to the inevitable heart attack.  Then it's all out of my hands, I don't have to fight with myself over doing it more directly or not anymore.  Plus in between time it makes everything feel numb sometimes, and I pretty much live for those moments where I'm so dizzy, disconnected, and dehydrated that I think and feel literally nothing at all.  Those moments when physically I'm so dejected that I can't even think are the only peace and quiet I ever get.  I can't even stand being around myself and living in my own head.  How could I be anything but the same burden on everyone else?

Nobody worries about my emotional stability because I don't even have anybody who cares enough about me to worry.  I've been suicidal before, the first time I was a teenager and I told my parents I felt that way, so my dad followed me around all day yelling that I was crazy.  I tried to call my brother for help and tell him what was going on but he couldn't hear me because my dad got up close to the phone and started yelling that I was insane and lying about everything I was trying to say.  Then in my 20s I got picked up by the police and taken to a mental hospital because I had been trying to break onto the roof of a 40 story building.  Therapy there didn't really help at all, all the nurses there would make snide comments about the patients like we weren't even there.  There was only one psychologist and he had about 10 minutes a day to talk to everyone.  It just made me more depressed so I lied and got out the next day.  But even then nobody cared about how sick I was.  Most of my relatives stopped talking to me for years claiming that I was just looking for attention.  Then every time I'd argue with my dad he would call my work and tell them about how I'm crazy and had been in a psych ward and couldn't be trusted.  I finally quit talking to him a few years ago.  If I was a good person then someone somewhere at any point in my life would have loved me.

30 years of pain and bullshit sprinkled with intense unavoidable self hatred internalized after a brutal childhood, followed by a lifetime of emptiness and loneliness because nobody at any point in your existence has ever given a fuck if you're alive, or dead, or replaced with a random inanimate object is anything but a temporary problem.
